glosses: To leave or withdraw from; to quit; to retire from.

examples.text: The soldiers evacuated the fortress.
The firefighters told us to evacuate the area as the flames approached.
The Norwegians were forced to evacuate the country.

glosses: To cause (or help) to leave or withdraw from.

examples.text: The firefighters decided to evacuate all the inhabitants from the street.

Early the next morning I set off on the long and hazardous trek through jungles and hills into Assam, and regretfully said "good-bye" to the gallant little Burma Railways, which had functioned to the last and played a big part in evacuating many thousands of refugees and wounded soldiers in the path of the rapidly advancing Japanese.

glosses: To make empty; to empty out; to remove the contents of, including to create a vacuum.

examples.text: The scientist evacuated the chamber before filling it with nitrogen.

glosses: To make empty; to deprive.

examples.text: Evacuate the Scriptures of their most important doctrines.

glosses: To remove; to eject; to void; to discharge, as the contents of a vessel, or of the bladder or the bowels (to stool).

examples.text: In the living state, the body is observed to receive aliment; to assimilate a part; to evacuate what is redundant or useless; [...]

glosses: To make void; to nullify; to vacate.

examples.text: to evacuate a contract or marriage
it would not evacuate a marriage after cohabitation and actual consummation

translations.source_sense_description: een gebouw of gebied voorgoed verlaten en leeg achterlaten

glosses: To move out of a dwelling or other property, either by choice or by eviction.

examples.text: I have to vacate my house by midday, as the new owner is moving in.
You are hereby ordered to vacate the premises within 14 days.
The dynamic tests at Wildenrath use continuous test tracks built on the site of a former Royal Air Force station that was vacated after the end of the Cold War.

glosses: To leave an office or position.

examples.text: He vacated his coaching position because of the corruption scandal.

glosses: To have a court judgement set aside; to annul.

examples.text: On Thursday, the New York court of appeals vacated his conviction after concluding that a trial judge permitted jurors to see and hear too much evidence not directly related to the charges he faced. It also erased his 23-year prison sentence and ordered a retrial.
The judge vacated the earlier decision when new evidence was presented.

glosses: To leave an area, usually as a result of orders from public authorities in the event of a riot or natural disaster.

examples.text: If you do not immediately vacate the area, we will make you leave with tear gas!
